$comment: RFX-111: every surviving mutant in a decision path is listed here with a reason, or the scheduled check fails. An entry names the package, the file, the line, the operator and why the survivor is acceptable.

justified.reason: Equivalent mutant: when two modes are equally strict, reassigning `strictest` to the same strictness changes no result; the function returns a mode, not which of two equal modes was seen first, and every mode of equal strictness is the same mode.

Unreachable by construction: a provider result exists only after `compiled` was assigned in the same try block, so the branch that guards `result.ok && compiled === undefined` cannot run; it is kept so that the types stay honest rather than asserted.

Equivalent mutant: a capture group of every secret pattern is non-empty by construction (each is bounded below by a quantifier), so `value === ""` is never true and the disjunction reduces to `value === undefined` either way.

Equivalent mutant: cutting a text of exactly the short length returns the text unchanged (`cut` keeps a text at or under its length), so treating the boundary as over or under yields the same request.
Equivalent mutant: the same boundary as line 140, for the objective; a text of exactly the short length is returned unchanged by `cut`.
Equivalent mutant: when two effects are equally restrictive they are the same effect, and reassigning `strictest` to it changes nothing that is returned.

Equivalent within the contract: the comparator differs only for two matches with the same rule id, whose relative order is not part of what a resolution promises; the deciding match is moved to the front regardless.
Equivalent within the contract: the same comparator, the other bound; only the order of two matches with the same rule id could change, and that order is not promised.
Equivalent mutant: when a declared default is exactly as strict as the one already kept, they are the same value, and keeping either yields the same compiled set.

Equivalent within the contract: `path_within` is accepted by the parser on the `path` field only, whose values are always text, and its expected value is always text; the guard against a non-string on either side is defensive and cannot be reached through a compiled policy.

Equivalent within the contract: the body of the guard at line 88, which cannot be reached through a compiled policy (`path_within` is accepted on the `path` field only, and both sides are always text).
Equivalent mutant: when the deciding match is already first, removing it and putting it back at the front is the identity; when there is none (-1), neither bound runs the move.

Equivalent mutant: trust is computed from the source (`entry.source === "project" ? entry.trusted : true`), so the literal on REFLEX's own source is never read; it is kept because the type asks for it and because it says what is true.
Equivalent mutant: one past the end reads as `""` through `?? ""`, which is not an option, so the loop ends there either way.

Differs only for httpie given a method and no URL (`http POST`), which contacts nothing: the original reads it as a read, the mutant as a write, and neither is a decision the corpus takes a position on. Any URL-bearing invocation is covered by tests.

Equivalent in effect: with the guard weakened, a non-string value reaches the pattern engine, which refuses anything but text and whose failure `CompiledPattern.test` turns into no match (`src/pattern.ts`), and a non-string expected value is refused by the parser; the guard says it in one place instead of relying on the engine.
